deities: Lord Shiva as Ramalingeswara (swayambhu linga, west-facing)

history.period: 1490-1509 CE (16th century; some local accounts cite 1460 CE)
history.summary: The Bugga Ramalingeswara Swamy Temple is a Vijayanagara-era Shiva shrine at Tadipatri in Anantapur district, Andhra Pradesh, on the southern bank of the Penna river. It was built between 1490 and 1509 CE by Pemmasani Ramalinga Nayudu I, chieftain of Gooty and Gandikota (local lore alternatively names the period of King Virupaksharaya, c. 1460 CE). Legend holds that the Shiva linga here was installed and worshipped by Rama (hence Ramalingeswara) to expiate the sin of killing the demon Tataka, and that sage Parasurama lived and meditated at the spot. 'Bugga' means a spring in Telugu: a perennial underground spring continuously bathes the swayambhu linga in the sanctum, the temple's signature feature. The architecture blends Chalukya, Chola and Vijayanagara styles, with the sanctum, ardhamandapa and mukhamandapa aligned, walls carved with scenes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and the Shiva Purana, famous saptaswara (musical) pillars that produce the seven notes of the scale, and unfinished gopurams described as 'wonders' by architectural historian James Fergusson. The west-facing linga is unusual. CORRECTION: the CSV lists town as 'Anantapur' - that is the district; the temple is at Tadipatri. Opening hours conflict across sources (6:00 AM-12:00 noon & 4:00-8:00 PM per devotee guides vs 6:00-11:30 AM & 5:00-7:30 PM per Incredible India) - verify locally.

name: Bugga Ramalingeswara Swamy Temple
town_description: Tadipatri is a town in Anantapur district, Andhra Pradesh, on the southern bank of the Penna river. It is known for its twin Vijayanagara-era temples - Chintala Venkataramana and Bugga Ramalingeswara - and has a railway station on the Gooty-Renigunta section, making it a convenient stopover for travellers to Gandikota and Belum.

travel.airport: Incredible India lists Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru, as the airport for this destination; Kadapa airport is about 112 km away (per a devotee travel blog).
travel.railway: Tadipatri railway station, about 4 km from the temple (Gooty-Renigunta line).
travel.road: About 1.6 km from Tadipatri bus stand; the temple lies on the southern bank of the Penna river, en route to the Chintala Venkataramana temple.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February (cooler months); Maha Shivaratri and Brahmotsavam are the main festival periods.
